cli.description: wev-skills: evidence-oriented orchestration for AI coding agents.
cli.help.lang: Message language (en or pt-BR). Defaults to WEV_LANG, then LANG.
cli.help.config: Path to a JSON configuration file.
cli.error.unexpected: Unexpected error. Set WEV_DEBUG=1 for a traceback.
cli.error.bad_result: The command returned a value that is not JSON serializable.
meta.config.validate.help: Validate a configuration file against the schema.
meta.config.validate.path: Path of the configuration file to validate.
hooks.help: Entry points for the Claude Code plugin hooks. Each reads the hook JSON on stdin (at most 1 MiB). Without a wev run for the directory or for the paths a command names, the brief hooks stay silent and the Bash pre-check judges the command under the built-in default policy; a problem in the pre-check becomes an 'ask', not silence. They never crash the session.
hooks.session-context.help: SessionStart hook: print the brief of the active run so the plan survives context compaction.
hooks.prompt-reminder.help: UserPromptSubmit hook: print the brief of the active run when harness.plan_reminder is on.
hooks.pre-tool-use.help: PreToolUse hook for the Bash tool: judge the command under the active run's pinned policy, or under the built-in default policy (execute mode, medium risk) when there is no run. It can deny or ask, never allow, and it never reads the approval store: the person's answer in Claude Code's permission prompt is the approval.
hooks.session.intro: wev: this is the recorded state of run {run}, not verified against the repository. Check the real state with 'wev run resume --run {run}' before continuing.
hooks.harness.help: Harness that sends the hook input and reads the answer (default: claude). Other harnesses have no ask decision for hooks: a policy 'ask' is allowed with a warning, a guard that cannot judge is denied.
hooks.reason.no_run_context: wev (no run, built-in default policy, {mode} mode): {reason}
hooks.reason.untokenizable: This command line cannot be analyzed safely (unbalanced quotes, command substitution, a here-document, a subshell or shell keywords), so a person decides.
hooks.reason.plan_shell: The run is in plan mode and this command line needs a shell (pipe, list or redirection), so it cannot be checked as one read-only command; a person decides.
hooks.error.input: The hook input is not a JSON object.
hooks.note.failed: wev hook {name}: the engine could not act ({error}).
hooks.reason.too_large: This command line is too long to analyze within the hook's time limit, so a person decides.
hooks.reason.unresolved: This command depends on the shell in a way that cannot be read here (a variable, $'...' quoting, a glob, a brace list or ~user), so what would run is unknown and a person decides: {command}
hooks.reason.environment: This command sets or changes environment variables or shell lookup for what runs next, which can change which program runs; a person decides (denied in plan mode): {command}
hooks.reason.assignment: This command line sets variables before a command ({names}). Variables such as PATH, GIT_* or DYLD_* change which program runs; a person decides (denied in plan mode).
hooks.reason.git_outside: git is pointed at a directory outside the run's root ({directory}); a person decides.
hooks.reason.directory_unknown: The working directory cannot be followed after an earlier part of this line (cd -, popd), so a person decides.
hooks.reason.engine_operator: This wev command is a human-operator decision (approval grant or deny, reopening, guard acknowledge, accepting or retiring a specialist lesson). Only the person may answer this prompt; an agent must not run it for itself.
hooks.reason.engine_run: This wev command starts or finishes a run, writes agent files or starts or stops a remote session, which changes what the run allows; a person decides.
hooks.reason.engine_request: This wev command files an approval request in the run's store; whether an action is asked for (again) is for a person to see, so a person decides.
hooks.reason.engine_config: This wev command names a configuration file on the command line; the policy in force is the run's pinned one, so a person decides.
hooks.reason.engine_jev: This wev command sends data to the JEV service (the content of a file it reads goes off this machine) and jev batch overwrites its --out file; a person decides.
hooks.reason.state_error: The recorded state of this run cannot be read ({error}); nothing can be checked, so a person decides. Inspect the state directory before continuing.
hooks.reason.internal_error: The engine failed while checking this command ({error}); it was not checked, so a person decides.
hooks.reason.registry_unreadable: wev: your run registry exists but cannot be read, so no run can be trusted; a person decides.
hooks.reason.unregistered_run: wev: a run was found in this tree but is not in your run registry; a person decides.
hooks.reason.unreadable_input: The hook input could not be read (too large or not valid JSON), so the command was not checked and a person decides.
hooks.reason.fail_safe_denied: the guard could not judge this command safely; this harness has no ask decision for hooks, so it was denied: {reason}
hooks.error.workdir: The directory this command names is not a string, or is not an existing directory, so it cannot be judged.
hooks.reason.ask_as_warning: wev would ask before this command; this harness cannot ask, so it was allowed: {reason}
hooks.reason.unknown_target: This command names a path through a variable, so its target cannot be known here, and a wev run is active in {root}. It may touch that run's tree, so a person decides.
orch.budget.warning: Run has used at least 80% of its engine budget; review the remaining scope.
orch.budget.stop: Run budget exhausted or the requested work would exceed it; start a new run with reviewed limits.
hooks.reason.engine_harness: This wev command installs or removes the wev package in a harness (it registers plugins and hooks in that harness's configuration); a person decides.
